note: On starting point he is the purest good-to-great case in this batch — ten years of consistent training, 20-22 sessions a month, self-rated effort of nine out of ten, and a want that is explicitly incremental: 'I want to look leaner and a little more chiseled.' He is the opposite of the stated exclusion. Successful is counted as a match on the equivalence clause: Bay Area technology professional, 41, two children, family savings. Two misses. Income fails on willingness and readiness rather than earnings — he budgeted around $300 a month, called $6,000 sticker shock, and needs his wife's agreement to draw on savings. Neglected health fails in the opposite direction from most of the corpus: his health is the area he manages best. Asked how he feels day to day he said 'I feel fantastic. There is no fatigue.' That is the finding worth carrying up. He satisfies the criterion the ICP treats as central and still did not buy, because meeting good-to-great with no crisis also means meeting it with no urgency. The manager named the same thing on the debrief an hour later — 'that's about a $300 a month problem'. If the corpus shows this pattern repeating, the stated ICP is selecting for prospects who are the easiest to like and the hardest to close.
